findings.finding: The page summary of ex-cm15-impact-check says 'the elastic case exchanges the velocities' for m₁=2 kg, m₂=6 kg and incoming velocities 3 and −1 m/s. The opened item, Example and Verification 2.1, correctly gives outgoing velocities −3 and +1 m/s: each velocity reverses. Exchanging them would give −1 and +3 m/s and total momentum 16 kg m/s instead of the initial zero.

The page says pthm-cm13-hamiltonian-field-integrates-the-model-equations 'identifies the integral curves … with the momentum-phase curves of the model’s motions, in every chart'. Its clause 1 gives Cartesian model-motion equivalence; clause 2 gives substituted Lagrange-equation equivalence for arbitrary generalized-coordinate maps. Lower-dimensional immersions require the separate ideal-constraint hypotheses for reconstruction as constrained model motions. The page's unrestricted summary is stronger than its supplier.

The page summary says the explicit angular factors are '1/√3' for both ⟨Y10,Q0Y00⟩ and ⟨Y1,±1,Q±Y00⟩. The opened example ex-nrqm-light-matter-hydrogen-dipole-angular-factors, clause (b) and Verification 2.1, correctly gives the latter pair as ∓1/√3, only their moduli being 1/√3. In particular the + entry is negative under the batch-37 harmonic and Q+ conventions.

The page summary says the matrices 'J_z e_m = m e_m and J_± e_m = ... on C^{2s+1} are self-adjoint'. The cited prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices clause (a) instead states J_+* = J_− and self-adjointness of J_z,J_x,J_y. For s=1/2, J_+ is the nonzero upper triangular matrix with only its upper-right entry equal to one, so it is not self-adjoint. The proposition itself states the correct result.

The page's spin-layer paragraph says that the displayed 'standard matrices J_z e_m=me_m and J_± e_m=√((s∓m)(s±m+1)) e_{m±1} ... are self-adjoint'. Its cited prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices clause (a) instead states J_+*=J_-; the self-adjoint operators are J_z,J_x,J_y. For s=1/2, J_+ is the matrix [[0,1],[0,0]], which is not self-adjoint. The page summary misstates its supplier.

The page summary says ex-nrqm-light-matter-two-level-dipole-drive-check 'computes the resonant co-rotating first-order amplitude dE0τ/(2ħ)'. The example's clause (b) correctly states this as |a+|. With its declared W=−dE0σx and initial time zero, the complex amplitude is i dE0τ/(2ħ). The summary should preserve the modulus distinction.

Page library/non-relativistic-quantum-mechanics-mathematics/qm-math-orbital-and-spin.md:62–65 describes the displayed Jz and J± matrices as 'self-adjoint'. The cited prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices, Statement (a), correctly asserts self-adjointness of Jz,Jx,Jy and J+*=J−. For s=1/2, J+ has matrix [[0,1],[0,0]], which is not self-adjoint. This is a false page-summary assertion; the supplying proposition is correct.
